$comment: UNACTIVATED Phase-1 design proposal for a future centralized MCP Registry manifest. This file is DATA plus an offline, read-only validator; it is NOT an executable workflow and is NOT wired into any publish pipeline. Nothing here publishes, registers, authenticates, or writes to any external service. There is currently NO live consumer: dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-core's live publish-mcp-registry.yml does NOT fetch this repo's manifest and does NOT run scripts/validate_mcp_manifest.py. The sha256 / version-domain / single-publisher rules below are offline integrity checks over this repo's own committed artifacts and a design contract for a future reviewed Phase-2 integration - they are NOT an enforceable gate on any live publish.

activation.$comment: All flags MUST remain false for this proposal. Wiring a consumer (e.g. having Core fetch mcp_registry/server.json at a pinned SHA, verify sha256, and run the validator before publishing) is a SEPARATE Phase-2 change: it needs hallong's explicit activation decision, its own independent review, and an end-to-end test proving the consumer reads the pinned content and verifies the sha256. This PR does not implement, enable, or authorize any of that.

manifest.$comment_integrity: Integrity is anchored to the sha256 of the committed mcp_registry/server.json in THIS repo, verified offline by check_integrity. There is deliberately NO source_ref pin claiming a publisher fetches this file: an earlier version pinned the PR base 1c24132, where mcp_registry/ did not exist, and no consumer has ever been wired. Do not add a consumer/fetch/source_ref claim without a reviewed Phase-2 change plus an end-to-end test.

official_schema.$comment_schema: Pinned official schema; validation is offline against the vendored copy so a moving upstream URL cannot change validation semantics.

baseline.$comment_baseline: Verbatim snapshot of dcc-mcp-core/server.json taken at authoring time. Used for backward-compatibility checks of every immutable field.

publisher.$comment_publisher: DESIGN DECLARATION (offline, NOT enforced on any live publish): the intended Phase-1 architecture has exactly ONE publisher. A second active publisher (e.g. an agent-plugins publish workflow) is a double-write hazard. check_single_publisher validates this invariant over this repo's own contract data only; it does NOT enforce who can actually publish, because no consumer is wired (see activation). Cross-repo GitHub Actions concurrency groups do NOT serialize across repositories, so they cannot be relied on to prevent two publishers from writing the same registry name.

immutable_fields.$comment_immutable: These fields MUST equal the Core baseline exactly. Brand fields (title, description, icons, websiteUrl) are intentionally centralized/owned here and are allowed to differ from Core; identity and wiring fields are not.
immutable_fields.name: io.github.dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-core
immutable_fields.packages[0].environmentVariables[0].name: DCC_MCP_GATEWAY_PORT
immutable_fields.$comment_repository: Per the official schema, repository is metadata about the SERVER SOURCE CODE. It MUST continue to point at dcc-mcp-core (the actual server source), NOT at the skills/agent-plugins repo. Repointing it to the skills repo is a schema/semantic violation and fails backward-compat.

version_domains.$comment_versions: STATIC AUTHORING-TIME values, NOT live-verified. Three independent version domains are validated SEPARATELY and never conflated. The offline validator checks self-consistency against these recorded values; it does NOT (and cannot, being stdlib-only and offline) query live PyPI wheels or the live Registry. 'Validation passed' here means static data integrity only - NOT dynamic/live version consistency. A change in one domain is not evidence for a change in another.

registry_metadata.$comment: STATIC authoring-time snapshot of server.json version + packages[0].version. In a live publish these are stamped by the Core release. value_in_source_manifest records the authoring value so check_version_domains can verify the source manifest has not drifted from the contract. The validator does NOT query the live Registry.

pypi_package.$comment: STATIC authoring-time value, NOT live-verified. The PyPI wheel dcc-mcp-server; ownership would be proven by the mcp-name marker in its published README. pypi_authoring_version(contract) reads value_at_authoring as the single source of truth for reporting and negative tests; the validator does NOT query live PyPI state.

plugin_suite.$comment: STATIC authoring-time value. The Agent Plugins Skills suite version, from plugins/dcc-mcp/plugin.json. Independent product line; NOT tied to the MCP server version.

rules: registry_metadata.version MUST equal registry_metadata.packages[0].version (they are stamped together at publish).
The source manifest version MUST equal registry_metadata.value_in_source_manifest (static authoring self-consistency, offline only).
A version mismatch between the manifest version and packages[0].version is a fail-stop error.
The plugin_suite version MUST NOT be written into server.json.version or packages[0].version (version-domain conflation is a fail-stop error).

The live Registry version (0.20.51) and the PyPI package version (0.20.53) are allowed to differ; this gap is the separate Core 0.20.53 re-release, explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this change. The validator does NOT verify either live value.

phase_2_plan.$comment_plan: DESIGN ONLY. Not implemented, not enabled, not executed in this phase. Documented so the switch can be reviewed when the time comes.
phase_2_plan.goal: Migrate the publisher role from dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-core to dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-agent-plugins so registration is managed where the manifest now lives.
required_ordering: 1. Land and review this contract + validator (Phase 1). Core remains the only entity that can mint the io.github.dcc-mcp/* OIDC token for the publisher.
2. Before switching, coordinate a single cutover: DISABLE the old Core publish-mcp-registry.yml release/dispatch triggers FIRST, then enable the new agent-plugins publisher.

3. Do NOT rely on cross-repo concurrency groups: they are per-repository and do not serialize writers in two different repos. Two simultaneously active publishers will double-write the same registry name.
4. Re-validate that exactly one active_publisher remains, that OIDC namespace ownership still resolves, and that no badge is attached before the new entry is queryable on the live registry.
blockers: OIDC publisher identity: the live publish workflow is gated on github.repository == 'dcc-mcp/dcc-mcp-core'; moving the publisher requires confirming the registry still accepts the io.github.dcc-mcp/* namespace from the new repo.

End-to-end test: no test currently proves a Core (or other) consumer actually reads mcp_registry/server.json at a pinned SHA and verifies its sha256 before publishing. Phase 2 MUST add this e2e test before any publisher cutover; until then this proposal provides NO enforceable publish gate.
Core 0.20.53 re-release is a separate publish-fix item and must not be bundled into this migration.
